reason: The cited evidence confirms that aging Al0.7CoCrFeNi forms coherent nanoscale L12 in the fcc phase and increases yield strength (E2, E3, E4). However, the evidence shows aging at 580 °C for 24 h, not 600–650 °C for 1–2 h, and none of the passages demonstrate that L12 precipitates improve ductility by acting as dislocation transmission bridges at lamellar boundaries; the ductility-enhancing mechanism is unsupported.
premises: L12 precipitates can form in the fcc lamellae of Al0.7CoCrFeNi upon low-temperature aging
These L12 precipitates are coherent and nanoscale
Coherent L12 precipitates increase yield strength
Coherent L12 precipitates can improve ductility by mitigating dislocation pile-ups at interfaces
Aging at 600–650 °C for 1–2 h is sufficient to form these beneficial precipitates
